searchText: +1, I think preserving "length compatibility" will probably prevent tooling from breaking in weird ways What do you mean by length compatibility? Like making new-style addresses also 42 chars, so tools that expect that length don't have to update I *suspect* that any tool that checks length also probably checks characters (e.g., `0x[a-zA-Z0-9]{40}` regexp). I also suggest a human readable prefix that identifies the chain (e.g. "eth"), so that people can't accidentally send things to Ethereum addresses on other chains like BSC. I'm confused, I thought that we were shooting for 32-byte addresses. Is this suggesting an encoding that targets 42 characters to stay inline with how long 20-byte addresses are in the `0x` hex format? This seems like the opposite of what I would expect since we would want a clear way to differentiate between new/old. Keeping them the same length seems to suggest some level of ambiguity in parsing. Most of the major security risks from Address Space Extension come from various permutations of attempting to use a long address as a legacy one. We should probably try to actively break anything that processes addresses as anything more than an opaque string. I suspect anyone who is storing an address in a fixed length buffer is parsing it to binary format first and will just have to update. Fair enough, that makes sense! Not a very strong opinion on my end I suggested bech32 addrs on ethresear.ch a while back but there wasn't a lot of interest would make the chain prefixes very natural and eliminate concerns around capitalization changing
